materialCapabilities.name: Paper and non-woven
materialCapabilities.appearance: Printed or plain, from a quiet texture to a large repeat.
materialCapabilities.joins: Seams are part of a hung wall. The match follows the repeat: free, straight or a half-drop. Half-drop papers and murals are set out on site; the calculator gives the order quantity, not the set-out.
materialCapabilities.care: Follow the maker. Many papers are not washable. We do not call a family washable, fire-rated or seamless unless that product’s own data says so.
materialCapabilities.handling: The wall has to be sound first. Lining is used when the maker or the wall requires it.
materialCapabilities.considerWhen: You want a printed pattern or a quieter, more even visual finish.
materialCapabilities.tradeoff: Print, backing and care vary substantially between products.
materialCapabilities.confirmBeforeOrdering: Confirm the repeat, match, usable width and actual cleaning instructions.
materialCapabilities.evidenceNote: Service and material guidance describe capability. Related service projects are context, not verified examples of every material family. The project dataset records the actual named products separately.

materialCapabilities.name: Grasscloth and natural weaves
materialCapabilities.appearance: Sisal, raffia, grass and other weaves. Colour and texture move from roll to roll.
materialCapabilities.joins: Seams show. The direction of the weave is agreed before the first length is cut.
materialCapabilities.care: Dry and gentle. Adhesive on the face marks the weave. Not a washable surface.
materialCapabilities.handling: Clean hands, an adhesive that suits the backing, and enough length from one batch to keep a wall together.
materialCapabilities.considerWhen: Natural fibre and a visible panel character are part of the look you want.
materialCapabilities.tradeoff: Adjacent drops can differ in shade; do not expect an invisible joint.
materialCapabilities.confirmBeforeOrdering: Review a full-wall example, panel layout and the exact care sheet.

deliveryStages.name: Surveying
deliveryStages.description: We measure on site, or from drawings when that is what the programme needs. Skirting, joinery, doors and windows come out of the area. What is left is the wall that will actually be hung.
paragraphs: We measure on site, or from drawings when that is what the programme needs. Skirting, joinery, doors and windows come out of the area. What is left is the wall that will actually be hung.

Quantities include wastage and pattern repeat. The allowance is typically 15–30%, depending on the pattern repeat and the layout, with staircases at the high end (around 30%) because of the angles. Extra rolls for pattern matching are confirmed at survey. A roll that looks generous on a plan can run short on the last pier.
The survey is also a judgement on the wall. If it is not ready for the material specified, we say so before anyone orders the last drop.

deliveryStages.name: Project management
deliveryStages.description: Every project has a project leader on the ground. That person is the day-to-day contact for the craft, the progress and the expectations that have been set.
paragraphs: Every project has a project leader on the ground. That person is the day-to-day contact for the craft, the progress and the expectations that have been set.

On a longer commission, senior oversight quality-controls the work and agrees a forward plan with you, in person, each week. Frequent and plain communication is part of the method, not a courtesy added at the end.

The team you meet on the first day is the core team that finishes. Disruption is kept low: work is contained, floors and joinery are protected, and the place is left tidy every evening. In a home we are visitors. In a hotel we work around the house.

deliveryStages.name: Supply
deliveryStages.description: On many hotel and flagship jobs the wallcovering is free-issue from the designer, the brand or the client. We manage delivery, check the delivery against the measure, and hang what was specified.
paragraphs: On many hotel and flagship jobs the wallcovering is free-issue from the designer, the brand or the client. We manage delivery, check the delivery against the measure, and hang what was specified.
We can also procure. Either way, the order has to cover the repeat and the wastage, or the last wall is the one that waits.
Delivery is timed to the hang. Paper sitting in a corridor for days is a risk to the goods and a nuisance to the building.

deliveryStages.name: Installation
deliveryStages.description: This is the craft the practice is built on. Wallcovering installation for hotels, retail flagships and prime residential rooms, including paper on joinery where the drawings show it.
paragraphs: This is the craft the practice is built on. Wallcovering installation for hotels, retail flagships and prime residential rooms, including paper on joinery where the drawings show it.

Preparation, where it is in the specification, includes stripping old paper, dustless sanding, and making good cracks and uneven surfaces. Some materials are specified with a lining paper. Some, including certain mural installs, are specified without one. We follow the specification.

Protection of floors, furniture and finished joinery is part of the hang, not an optional extra. Where Mr Wallcover is appointed as main decorating contractor, the package can include fine painting, French polishing and other specialist finishes, as it did at Brown's Hotel, Mayfair.

deliveryStages.name: Aftercare
deliveryStages.description: Aftercare is the fifth part of the service. A return inspection is included once the paper has settled, about four to six weeks after completion. Seams and edges are attended to. There is a priority repair call-out for the workmanship, and a twelve-month guarantee.
paragraphs: Aftercare is the fifth part of the service. A return inspection is included once the paper has settled, about four to six weeks after completion. Seams and edges are attended to. There is a priority repair call-out for the workmanship, and a twelve-month guarantee.
The detail, including care by material and what the guarantee does not cover, is on the aftercare page.

aftercare.introduction: Aftercare is one of the five parts of a Mr Wallcover commission. The return visit is included, and the twelve-month workmanship guarantee is set out below.

inspection.title: Return inspection
paragraphs: About four to six weeks after we finish, we come back. By then the heating, the ventilation and the humidity have had a chance to move the paper. That movement is settling. It is the reason for the visit.
We look at seams, edges, corners and any joinery that was covered. Touch-ups that belong to the hang are done on that visit. There is no call-out charge for this inspection.

seams.title: Seams and edges
paragraphs: A seam that opens, or an edge that lifts, because of the way the material was hung, is our work to put right. We re-adhere, trim and touch in. We do not paint over a problem and hope the light is kind.

Natural seams in grasscloth, silk and hand-painted goods are a property of the material. We will have said so before the hang. Those are not faults. A seam that has let go is different, and we treat it as such.

callout.title: Priority repair call-out
paragraphs: During the guarantee, a call about our own workmanship comes ahead of new enquiries. The contact page is the quickest way. A photograph helps us see whether we are looking at the hang, a knock, or the building.
If it is the hang, we book the return as a priority. If it is the building, we will say that plainly rather than charge you for a repair that will fail again.

humidity.title: Humidity and settling
paragraphs: Paper and textile move with the moisture in the room. A new hang will ease as it dries, and it may ease again when the heating season starts or when a closed room is opened to damp weather. That is ordinary. It is why the return visit waits four to six weeks, rather than the next morning.

Keep the heat steady and the room ventilated. A cold, damp wall, a leak above a ceiling, or a fan heater pointed at one seam is how edges lift. Do not steam-clean wallcoverings. Do not sit a humidifier against the paper.
If a stain spreads, or a wall feels cold and soft, look for damp before you look for a decorator. We would rather be called early than asked to hang the same wall twice over a wet substrate.

guarantee.title: Twelve-month workmanship guarantee
paragraphs: For twelve months from completion, Mr Wallcover guarantees the workmanship of the hang. That covers seams opening, edges lifting, and adhesive failure that comes from the way we hung the material.
It does not cover building movement, damp, leaks, or a substrate that fails. It does not cover damage by later trades, impact, furniture, or cleaning the material cannot take.
Some people call this a warranty. It is the same promise: twelve months on our workmanship, and a clear line where the building takes over from the hang.

care.title: Care and cleaning
care.intro: This is general guidance for the materials we hang. Where the maker has issued a care note, that note leads. When a mark appears, stop. Household cleaners, steam and magic sponges are how a small mark becomes a large one.

items.title: Silk
items.text: Dust with a clean, dry, soft cloth. No water, no solvent, no steam. A stain needs a conservator, not a detergent. Keep handbags, chair backs and sun off the cloth where you can.

items.title: Grasscloth and natural weaves
items.text: Dry dust only, and lightly. Moisture stains grasscloth and can swell the weave. Seams and variation in colour are part of the material. Do not try to scrub them even.

items.title: Fabric walling
items.text: Vacuum on a low suction with a soft brush head, if the maker allows it. Do not soak the textile. Spot treatment belongs to a specialist, tested somewhere that will not show.

items.title: Vinyl and contract wallcoverings
items.text: Wipe with a barely damp cloth and a drop of mild soap, then dry. No abrasive creams, no neat bleach, no scourers. Contract vinyl will take more than silk. It will not take a careless bucket.

items.title: Hand-painted papers
items.text: No liquids on the surface. Dust dry, and rarely. Direct sun fades a scenic paper unevenly. Marks, flaking and water damage need a paper conservator. We can help you find the right person. We will not experiment on a de Gournay or Fromental-style panel.

items.title: Murals
items.text: Follow the maker's care note for that print or that hand-made piece. Do not use household spray cleaner. If a panel is damaged, photograph it and call us before anyone tries to patch it.

items.title: Acoustic wallcoverings and panels
items.text: Vacuum dust from the face with low suction and a soft head. Do not soak the fabric or the perforations. Water and heavy adhesive at the edge can close the surface the panel was specified to keep open.

aftercare.existingPaperNote: For wallcoverings installed by others, send photographs for an assessment of whether a repair is possible. The Mr Wallcover workmanship guarantee applies to its own installation; it does not transfer to an existing hang by another installer.

instructions: Leave unknown values null and keep unanswered questions in questionsForThePractice.
